column1: #   url       https git URL, or "alias:<tier>/<dir>" to point at another clone,

column1: # domain/ : travel, hospitality and discovery product references. Not installed.
#           These answer "what does a real travel product actually do?" - the
#           questions a spec cannot, which is what stops us reinventing wheels.

column4: THE reference for multi-modal routing. RAPTOR transit algorithm over GTFS combined with street walking/biking/car. This is the honest answer to Mumbai's train-vs-car problem, and the model our travel.ts facade is shaped around.

Event ticketing done properly: capacity-limited availability, vouchers/quota rules, order state machines, and a separate presale (buyer) vs eventbox (organiser) app split. The reference for our provider-side booking loop.
Self-hosted travel planner, TypeScript, 14k stars, actively developed. Reference for trip collaboration, itinerary UX, and a comparable TS stack.
Self-hostable travel tracker and trip planner. Reference for the visit/place/segment data model and itinerary timeline UX.
Minimalist POI map tracker and trip planner, self-hosted, MIT. Reference for a deliberately narrow scope: map, POIs, trip log.
Travellers community for hosting and meeting people. Reference for the traveller-to-local matching half of the marketplace, including trust and reputation mechanics.
Non-profit hospitality network: hosts and travellers connecting, plus find-a-stay. Reference for trust, verification and community signalling on both sides of our marketplace.

column1: # data/ : POI data semantics, geocoding and retrieval. The layer that decides
#         what we can honestly store, query and rank.

column4: Authoritative OSM tagging schema. Defines the exact semantics of the tags our harvest depends on - opening_hours grammar, wheelchair, fee, capacity, cuisine, diet:*, indoor. This is what our zod schemas must match.
5.8k stars, the standard library for downloading and modelling OSM data by bbox or polygon. Reference for query construction, tag filters and network caching in our harvest scripts.
Routing engine with isochrone generation, GTFS transit import and custom time-dependent weighting. Reference for our congestion multiplier and isochrone-first filtering.
Self-hostable geocoder (MIT), the usual alternative to depending on Nominatim's public instance. Fallback for our address and place search.
Lightweight OSM geocoder (Apache-2.0). Second geocoder option, simpler to self-host than Pelias.
11k stars, in-process full-text search for JS/TS with typo tolerance and faceting. The live alternative to SQLite FTS5 in our retrieval stage - we compare the two before committing.
Catalogue of open travel/tourism data sources. The repo is 2 GB of data files so we take the README, which is the list we actually wanted. Cited, not installed.

column1: # peer/ : hackathon and AI travel-planner projects. Most are small and
#          low-star, so read them for TECHNIQUES and for the competitive
#          landscape, not as engineering exemplars. Each row names the one

column4: HIGHEST CONCEPTUAL RELEVANCE. A deterministic itinerary engine with web research and OPTIONAL AI on top - the same split we chose (LLM never in the decision path). Check how it structures the engine/LLM boundary.
RAG + embeddings + OR-Tools + Google Maps. Our reference for how people actually wire a real constraint solver into a travel app, and where the seams are.
FastAPI + structured LLM output + preferences + ACCESSIBILITY. Accessibility is a graded PS factor and the one OSM barely populates. MIT.
Agentic planning with tools, memory and Supabase/pgvector. Reference for the memory layer and for how they scope agent tools. MIT, TypeScript.
79 stars. LangGraph + POI retrieval + ROUTE CLUSTERING + LLM itinerary. Their route clustering is the closest prior art to our packer.
81 stars, 2023, mostly retired. A plain GPT-itinerary baseline. Useful as the 'naive LLM' comparison point in our write-up.
Conversational travel agent covering routes, budget, hotels and restaurants. Reference for conversational UX and budget handling.
LangGraph with tools, memory, streaming and structured trip cards. Reference for streaming structured output over SSE.
Tiny (19 KB) LangGraph multi-agent planner. Useful only to see the multi-agent pattern we are deliberately NOT using, and why.
Multi-agent planner with geolocation and India-focused travel dialogue. India-specific phrasing and intent patterns worth borrowing for NLU fixtures.

column1: # systems/ : published, code-released research systems that solve THIS problem.
#            The strongest tier. Cite these in the deck and read them before
#            designing anything they already solved. (Names taken from
#            ATHITI_MASTERPLAN_V2.md, verified against the GitHub API.)

column4: ACM SIGSPATIAL 2025. Four-stage pipeline: UGC -> structured Landscape/Activity/Atmosphere extraction -> dimension-aware retrieval -> LLM rerank -> cluster-aware spatial optimisation. Gives us our perception-dimension schema and per-dimension retrieval instead of one blended embedding.

arXiv 2402.07204, DEPLOYED IN PRODUCTION at the TuTu travel service with thousands of real users. Request Decomposition (granularity x specificity x attitude) plus cluster-then-route spatial optimisation. The production-validated source for our soft-constraint fields and our packing strategy. GPL-3.0.

LLM + Z3 SMT hybrid planner, including z3_temporal_scheduler_with_relaxation.py. THE upgrade over hand-rolled constraint assertions: a real satisfiability proof plus an unsat core that yields automatic minimal relaxation. Directly generates our relaxation ladder algorithmically.

TripCraft, ACL 2025 Main (Microsoft + IIT Bhubaneswar). The constraint-aware travel planning benchmark. Source of our five continuous evaluation metrics: Temporal, Attraction, Spatial, Ordering, Persona scores.

NTT Research. Persona-instantiated LLM agents hold a structured discussion to reach group consensus, instead of statically averaging preference vectors. The upgrade path for our group/traveler-type handling.

Local-first planner with a "Trip Stress Radar" scoring overload / rain-risk / anchor-pressure / transit-complexity 0-100 with concrete suggested fixes. Cleanest existing framing of a fatigue and buffer model. MIT.

Multi-agent travel system: Supervisor Agent decomposes the query, Domain Guardrails filter unsafe or off-topic input, specialist sub-agents per domain, human-in-the-loop approval gate. Reference for our input-safety layer and orchestration shape. MIT.

Gemini-based planner with explicit pipeline nodes (Places -> Route -> Cost -> Synthesizer). Concrete shipped evidence that the staged-pipeline pattern is implementable, which is the core of our architecture claim.

Academic capstone folding an ML-predicted crowd "Busyness Index" into itinerary scoring. Sourceable method for our crowd_fit ranking feature, which the plan needs grounding for. GPL-2.0, and a 387 MB repo so only the model and service code is kept.

RAG + embeddings + OR-Tools + Google Maps. The masterplan flags this as a modest-scope project we should NOT quote as a benchmark without checking ourselves. Kept as a counter-example, not an authority.
Academic hybrid content-based/collaborative-filtering tourism recommender. Useful ONLY as a baseline-quality comparison: static catalogue, no real-time constraints, same cold-start problem. GPL-3.0.

column1: # Additional peer references added from the team list

column4: 50 stars, classic content/collaborative-filtering tourism recommender over a Kaggle-style attraction dataset. Baseline comparison, not an architecture reference.
Notebook-based tourism recommendation system. 153 MB almost entirely dataset, so only the notebooks and code are kept.
Small FastAPI-style AI travel assistant with an input.json and a generated report.md. Useful for comparing how a thin LLM wrapper differs from our engine-first design.
The Xaler1/TREK original named in the masterplan, kept alongside liketrek/TREK (the actively developed 14k-star fork we already have) so we can see what the fork diverged on. AGPL-3.0.
